L2t: Courts interpret restrictive covenants in subdivision plats by looking at the language used and the apparent purpose of the restriction, resolving doubts in light of the overall development scheme.
L3t: A covenant limiting structures to 'dwelling purposes' is read as restricting how a building is used, not merely what kind of building is erected, since the evident purpose is to keep the subdivision residential.
L4t: The court will likely grant the injunction, because the restriction was meant to keep the subdivision residential and so bars converting the dwelling into a dental office.
L2f: Courts generally treat plat restrictions as unenforceable by neighboring lot owners unless each owner personally signed the original covenant document.
L3f: The covenant's phrase 'no structure shall be built' is read literally as governing only the act of construction, so it regulates what may be built and says nothing about the use of a building once it exists.
L4f: The court will likely deny the injunction, because the restriction only limits what may be built and not later use, so the owner may use the dwelling as a dental office.
cand_true: Grant the injunction; the restriction requires residential use only
cand_wrong1: Deny the injunction; the restriction governs only construction, not later use
cand_wrong2: Deny the injunction because covenants restricting land use are disfavored and a dental office is a minor, harmless change
